headline: High: shared filesystem/MCP and overlapping write surfaces make prompt injection, data leakage, and state corruption plausible by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code reads/writes repo files and uses MCP; OpenBBTerminal also uses MCP and consumes files via Python environments. That creates a plausible bridge where content from one can be fed into the other, especially through shared files or MCP outputs. The pathway is not proven, but uncertainty favors the higher severity.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same workspace or MCP server outputs are copied into files the other reads, injection becomes reachable.
IF OpenBBTerminal treats MCP/file content as instructions or parameters, attacker-controlled text can steer Claude Code.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and MCP endpoints per agent.
Disable MCP on one side for the test run.
Use a manual review step before Claude Code consumes OpenBB outputs.
Prefix all inter-agent handoffs with a fixed schema and reject free-form instructions.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging to shared artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and files in cwd, while OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data. If they share a workspace or files, sensitive code or financial data can cross boundaries. OpenBBTerminal’s network/API surfaces and Claude Code’s broad egress increase exposure, though the exact flow is not fully documented.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same directory or exchanged files contain secrets, leakage is reachable.
IF OpenBBTerminal sends loaded financial data to remote APIs, data can leave the local boundary.
mitigations: Use separate directories and credentials for each agent.
Remove secrets from shared files before handoff.
Run OpenBBTerminal on synthetic or public-only datasets.
Audit outbound requests during the session.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent access controls at the filesystem layer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code can write the filesystem, modify git state, and spawn subprocesses; OpenBBTerminal can use MCP and connect to localhost services. If both touch the same repo or mutable resource, concurrent writes and state drift are plausible. Because Claude Code explicitly shares state via filesystem and git, the conflict is dangerous by default when paired with another mutable tool.
conditions: IF both agents modify the same git branch or files without locking, conflicts and lost updates occur.
IF OpenBBTerminal writes through MCP into a shared mutable backend, concurrent mutation becomes reachable.
mitigations: Assign separate branches or working trees.
Serialize writes with a lock file or single-writer rule.
Disable one agent’s write path during the other’s run.
Review git diffs before merge.
requires-engineering: add transactional locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can generate code, shell commands, and file edits that OpenBBTerminal could ingest through files or MCP. OpenBBTerminal then operates on financial workflows and APIs, so unverified upstream output can cascade into incorrect analysis or actions. The pair lacks any documented verification boundary in the profiles, so the safer choice is medium.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal consumes Claude Code output as parameters or prompts without validation, errors propagate.
IF Claude Code writes a script or config that OpenBBTerminal executes, downstream actions can be wrong.
mitigations: Require schema validation on all handoffs.
Add a human review step before execution.
Use read-only mode for OpenBBTerminal when consuming Claude output.
Log and diff every generated artifact.
requires-engineering: implement typed contracts between agents.

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code handles git credentials and local source code, while OpenBBTerminal handles financial and licensed data. If regulated financial or licensed datasets are placed into Claude Code’s workspace, residency/retention and licensing obligations may diverge from OpenBBTerminal’s handling. The profiles do not prove a specific breach, but the mismatch is plausible enough for medium.
conditions: IF regulated financial data is copied into Claude Code’s workspace, its retention/logging may differ from OpenBBTerminal’s.
IF licensed data is shared across both agents, license terms may be violated by the handoff.
mitigations: Keep regulated datasets out of Claude Code workspaces.
Use public or synthetic data for cross-agent testing.
Review retention settings before sharing outputs.
Document data-class boundaries for each agent.
requires-engineering: map each data class to an approved processing policy.
